quick: May be taken with or without food, at the same time each day
Not recommended; avoid unless clearly necessary
Avoid - likely excreted in milk; not recommended
Contraindicated in moderate-severe (Child-Pugh B/C); caution in mild
No clinically relevant interaction with a single drink; limit excess
summary: Roflumilast is an oral selective PDE4 inhibitor used to reduce the risk of exacerbations in severe COPD associated with chronic bronchitis and a history of exacerbations. It is anti-inflammatory rather than a bronchodilator and is not for acute bronchospasm. Key tolerability issues are weight loss, diarrhea, nausea, and psychiatric effects including mood changes and suicidality; it is contraindicated in moderate to severe hepatic impairment.
indications: To reduce the risk of COPD exacerbations in patients with severe COPD associated with chronic bronchitis and a history of exacerbations

dosage.n: Maintenance dose; not for acute bronchospasm

dosage.d: 250 mcg once daily for 4 weeks, then 500 mcg once daily
dosage.n: 250 mcg is a starter dose, not therapeutic; reduces discontinuation

admin: Take one tablet once daily with or without food
Take at approximately the same time each day
Do not use to relieve sudden breathing problems (acute bronchospasm)
Continue other prescribed COPD therapies (bronchodilators) as directed
moa: Roflumilast and its active N-oxide metabolite are selective inhibitors of phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4), the major cyclic AMP-metabolizing enzyme in lung inflammatory and structural cells. Inhibition raises intracellular cyclic AMP, dampening inflammatory cell activity (neutrophils, macrophages, T cells). The net effect is reduced airway inflammation in COPD rather than direct bronchodilation.

absolute: Moderate to severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh B or C)
relative: History of depression with suicidal ideation or behavior
Low body weight or risk of significant weight loss
Use with strong CYP3A4 inducers (reduced efficacy)

preg: There are limited data in pregnant women; roflumilast is generally not recommended during pregnancy and should be used only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: Available data in animals show excretion into milk; breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in moderate to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C). In mild impairment (Child-Pugh A) the increase in exposure is not considered clinically relevant, but use with caution.

major: Strong CYP3A4/1A2 inhibitors (e.g., fluvoxamine, enoxacin, cimetidine) - increase roflumilast exposure and adverse effects
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin) - reduce efficacy; concomitant use not recommended
moderate: Oral contraceptives containing gestodene and ethinylestradiol (increase roflumilast exposure)
interactions.food: Food does not affect the overall extent of absorption; may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: A single dose of alcohol had no clinically relevant interaction; avoid heavy use

serious: Psychiatric events: depression, anxiety, suicidal thoughts or behavior

monitoring: Body weight at regular intervals; evaluate and consider discontinuation if significant loss
Mood and behavior - new or worsening depression, anxiety, or suicidal thoughts
Gastrointestinal symptoms and hydration in the first weeks of therapy
counsel: This medicine prevents flare-ups; it does not relieve sudden breathing trouble
Watch for and report new or worsening mood changes, anxiety, or thoughts of self-harm
Diarrhea, nausea, and weight loss are common early and often improve - report large weight loss
Take it once daily at the same time; continue your other inhalers
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially for seizures, TB, or infections
pk: Anti-inflammatory effect develops over days to weeks of regular dosing
Roflumilast peak ~1 hour; active N-oxide metabolite peaks ~8 hours
pearls: Anti-inflammatory PDE4 inhibitor - NOT a bronchodilator and NOT for acute bronchospasm
Weight loss and GI effects are the main early tolerability problems; consider 250 mcg run-in
Screen for and monitor depression/suicidality before and during treatment
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose - do not double up.
overdose: Symptoms after supratherapeutic doses in studies included headache, gastrointestinal disorders, dizziness, palpitations, lightheadedness, clamminess, and hypotension. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive. Because roflumilast is highly protein bound, dialysis is unlikely to remove significant amounts.
